prompt.context: We run a manufacturing business in the Southeastern U.S. and have a number of salespeople who are consistently reimbursed for gas. We would like to determine how much we spent on gasoline last year so that we can evaluate how the rising cost of gasoline will impact our bottom line.
prompt.question: Question 1: What was the cost of gas last year? Question 2: How will our expenses be affected going forward? Question 3: Do you have any recommendations on what we can do to curb our expenses?

clarifying_info.q: How many salespeople do we have?
clarifying_info.a: 30 salespeople spread throughout the country, in 3 regions (East, Central, West) with 10 per region.

clarifying_info.q: How much does a typical salesperson drive?
clarifying_info.a: There are three driver categories: low (500 miles/week), medium (1000 miles/week), and high (1500 miles/week). There are 5 low, 15 medium, and 10 high mileage drivers.

clarifying_info.q: Are salespeople reimbursed for personal use?
clarifying_info.a: Not supposed to be, but it happens.

clarifying_info.q: What is the fuel efficiency of the vehicles?
Are there other gasoline uses such as delivery trucks or factory machines?
clarifying_info.a: There are, but don't worry about them for this case.

clarifying_info.q: What is the gas price to use?
clarifying_info.a: Assume an average gas price over the given period (candidate makes the assumption).

clarifying_info.q: Are there any changes planned for the sales force going forward?
clarifying_info.a: No change in habits or mileage planned for the coming year.

framework: Determine total annual miles driven by the sales force (broken down by driver category)
Convert miles to gallons using vehicle fuel efficiency
Apply an assumed gas price to calculate total cost for the prior year
Optionally break prior year into quarters to capture different gas price levels throughout the year
Build in a cushion for personal usage that slips through reimbursement controls
Project forward under three scenarios (best, worst, most likely) based on assumed gas price changes
Generate out-of-the-box recommendations to curb expenses

questions.prompt: Question 1: Calculate the total gasoline cost for the sales force last year.
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment the 30 salespeople into the three mileage tiers, compute total weekly miles, annualize, divide by MPG to get gallons, then multiply by an assumed gas price. A strong answer also builds in a personal-use cushion. Breaking the year into quarters (to reflect seasonal price variation) is a plus. A table layout earns extra credit.

math.setup: 5 low @ 500 mi/wk, 15 medium @ 1000 mi/wk, 10 high @ 1500 mi/wk. 30 mpg. Assume ~$3/gal (candidate assumption). 52 weeks/year. Personal-use cushion ~10%.
math.answer: Approximately $169,000–$186,000 depending on personal-use cushion, at $3/gallon assumption. Candidate should state their gas price assumption clearly.

questions.prompt: Question 2: How will expenses be affected going forward given the rising cost of gasoline?
questions.guidance: Candidate should develop three scenarios (best, worst, most likely) for future gas prices and translate each into a projected annual cost using the same mileage base (no change in habits or headcount). The answer should quantify the dollar impact of each scenario and note the range of exposure.

math.setup: Same annual mileage base: 1,690,000 miles / 30 mpg = 56,333 gallons. Model three price scenarios.
steps: Year-over-year change vs. $3 base: best = -$28K, most likely = +$28K, worst = +$84K (before personal-use cushion)
math.answer: Expense range of roughly $141K–$254K depending on gas price scenario, implying up to ~$85K upside risk versus the prior-year baseline.

questions.prompt: Question 3: What recommendations would you make to curb gasoline expenses?
questions.guidance: Looking for out-of-the-box, creative, and implementable suggestions. A strong answer organizes ideas into logical categories and mentions how to implement them.

brainstorming.prompt: What recommendations would you make to reduce or control the company's gasoline reimbursement expenses?

categories.name: Policy & Controls
ideas: Set per-mile or per-week reimbursement caps
Reimburse for only one octane level (regular unleaded)
Require trip logs / mileage reporting for all reimbursements
Audit reimbursement claims against GPS or odometer data
Define and enforce a clear policy on personal-use exclusion

categories.name: Financial Hedging
ideas: Purchase oil futures or options to hedge against price spikes
Lock in fleet fuel contracts with suppliers at fixed rates
Evaluate fleet fuel cards that offer volume discounts

categories.name: Fleet & Efficiency
ideas: Issue company gas cards for centralized visibility and spending control
Transition to higher-MPG or hybrid vehicles to reduce gallons consumed
Optimize sales territories to minimize unnecessary driving
Encourage route planning tools (GPS, mapping software) to cut redundant miles

categories.name: Behavioral & Structural
ideas: Increase use of video conferencing / virtual sales calls to reduce driving
Offer incentives for carpooling between salespeople in the same region
Consider realigning territories so low-traffic regions use low-mileage drivers

categories.name: Alternative Models
ideas: Explore car allowance programs instead of per-mile reimbursement to shift price risk to employees
Evaluate leasing an electric-vehicle fleet for applicable routes

recommendation: The company spent approximately $169K–$186K on salesforce gasoline last year (at a ~$3/gal assumption), and faces exposure of up to ~$253K if prices reach $4.50/gal with no behavioral changes.

Priority actions: (1) implement a gas card program for spending visibility and volume discounts, (2) set clear reimbursement policies with mileage caps and personal-use exclusion enforcement, and (3) evaluate a fuel-price hedging strategy to reduce worst-case scenario risk.
risks: Gas prices could spike beyond modeled worst case, increasing exposure further
Tighter controls on personal use may affect sales force morale or retention
Hedging strategies carry their own financial risk if prices fall
next_steps: Conduct a detailed audit of last year's reimbursement records to validate assumptions
Issue RFPs for fleet fuel card programs
Consult treasury/finance on feasibility of fuel price hedging
Pilot a route-optimization tool with one region and measure mileage reduction
